title: Flipkart to Launch Food Delivery in Coming Weeks, Says Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy
excerpt: The Walmart-backed e-commerce giant is set to enter India's $9 billion food delivery market, leveraging its Flipkart Minutes quick-commerce infrastructure as part of an aggressive pre-IPO diversification push.
body:
• Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy has confirmed the company will launch its food delivery service in the coming weeks, starting with a pilot in Bengaluru.
  • The move pits Flipkart directly against the Zomato-Swiggy duopoly in India's $9 billion food delivery market, projected to reach $24 billion by FY30.
  • Flipkart plans to leverage its 800-plus Flipkart Minutes dark stores and existing logistics network to power the new service.
  • The food delivery push is part of a broader pre-IPO diversification strategy that also includes ticketing and a standalone quick-commerce app.

Flipkart Confirms Food Delivery Is Imminent

Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy has confirmed that the Walmart-owned e-commerce giant will launch its food delivery service within the coming weeks, according to multiple reports. The announcement marks a decisive step after months of planning and team-building, bringing Flipkart into direct competition with Zomato and Swiggy in one of India's most fiercely contested consumer markets.

https://x.com/CNBCTV18Live/status/2080513916820693224

The company has been evaluating the food delivery segment since early 2026, when reports first emerged of a planned pilot in Bengaluru around May-June. Krishnamurthy's statement signals that Flipkart has moved past the evaluation stage and is ready for a live launch, with a wider national rollout expected by late 2026 or early 2027, according to The Economic Times.

"Flipkart is evaluating the food delivery market while trying to identify a differentiated positioning in the space."

— Source familiar with Flipkart's plans, per The Economic Times

Challenging the Zomato-Swiggy Duopoly

India's online food delivery market is estimated at approximately $9 billion in FY25 and is projected to grow to roughly $24 billion by FY30, according to brokerage firm Jefferies. The segment is effectively a near-duopoly, with Zomato, owned by Eternal and Swiggy commanding the vast majority of market share. When Flipkart's food delivery plans first surfaced in February, shares of both Eternal and Swiggy fell up to 3 percent, according to Restaurant India.

The market has a graveyard of failed entrants. Uber Eats shut down its India operations in 2020. Ola made multiple attempts through Ola Cafes, the acquisition of Foodpanda, and its Ola Dash quick-delivery service — all of which were eventually discontinued. But the segment has also attracted newer challengers: ride-hailing unicorn Rapido launched its food delivery platform Ownly, while quick-commerce players have introduced food verticals including Blinkit's Bistro, Zepto Cafe, and Swiggy's own Bolt and Snacc sub-brands.

Flipkart Minutes: The Logistics Advantage

Flipkart's primary competitive edge is its existing quick-commerce infrastructure. Flipkart Minutes, launched in September 2023 as a 10-minute grocery delivery service, has scaled rapidly to over 800 dark stores across India, adding roughly 100 new stores each month. The company has been targeting 1,200 dark stores by mid-2026 with expansion to 250 cities.

This network of hyperlocal fulfilment centres gives Flipkart a ready-made logistics backbone for food delivery — a critical factor in a business where speed and delivery radius determine viability. The company is also planning to spin out Flipkart Minutes into a standalone app ahead of the Big Billion Days festive sale, following the playbook that Swiggy used when it separated Instamart into its own app in January 2025.

Flipkart is reportedly evaluating two routes for the food delivery launch: building its own standalone platform or launching a buyer-side application on the government-backed Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), similar to the approach taken by Ola and Paytm. The ONDC route would significantly reduce restaurant onboarding costs, letting Flipkart focus on the consumer interface and delivery logistics. The company had explored an ONDC-based entry into food delivery in 2024, but those plans did not advance beyond the planning stage.

What It Means for Indians Abroad

For NRIs who track Indian market movements, Flipkart's entry reshapes the investment landscape around India's food delivery sector. Zomato (through parent company Eternal) and Swiggy are both publicly listed, and their stock prices have already shown sensitivity to Flipkart's plans. A well-funded, infrastructure-rich third entrant could compress margins across the sector while potentially benefiting consumers with lower prices and more choices — a shift worth watching for anyone with Indian tech exposure in their portfolio.

The IPO Calculus

Every move Flipkart makes needs to be understood through the lens of its impending IPO. The company is widely expected to file for a public listing in late 2026 or early 2027, and food delivery represents a high-frequency use case that could boost daily active users and demonstrate platform stickiness to public market investors. Flipkart's marketplace arm reported operating revenue of ₹20,493 crore in FY25, up 14.4 percent year-on-year, while net losses declined 37 percent to ₹1,494 crore.

But the strategy carries risk. Under Krishnamurthy, Flipkart is simultaneously preparing an IPO, launching food delivery, entering ticketing, and spinning out a standalone quick-commerce app. Companies that spread too thin before a public listing often find that nothing is executed well enough to impress investors. Whether Flipkart can build India's most complete consumer platform — or is simply adding features to inflate its IPO valuation — will become clearer in the coming weeks as the food delivery pilot goes live.
